hypothesis: In North Sea plaice (Pleuronectes platessa), mean condition factor K = 100·W/L^3 computed in length classes is non-constant, increasing to a single interior maximum near 30 cm total length and then declining slowly at larger sizes.
pass_criterion: Using individual plaice with measured length and weight, mean K per 2-cm length class (classes with n>=30) shows (a) a maximum class lying between 26 and 34 cm, (b) K at the maximum exceeds mean K of the 10-18 cm classes by >=5% and mean K of the largest classes (>=45 cm, or the top 3 populated classes) by >=3%, with bootstrap 95% CIs of the differences excluding 0, and (c) a piecewise/quadratic fit of K on length has a significant negative curvature (p<0.01) with vertex between 26 and 34 cm. Results must hold in the pooled data and in at least 2 of 3 separate survey-year groups.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any of: the maximum-K length class lies outside 26-34 cm; K varies by less than 5% between its maximum and the 10-18 cm classes; K at >=45 cm is not at least 3% lower than the maximum (including monotonic increase with size); or the quadratic curvature is non-significant or positive (p>=0.01); in the pooled data or in fewer than 2 of 3 year groups.
interpretation: Thompson's k = W/L^3 is the Fulton condition factor (usually scaled by 100, units g/cm^3). 'Size of sexual maturity' is taken as roughly 30 cm (his stated value), the first-maturity length of North Sea plaice. Modern reinterpretation: trawl-survey weights are fresh whole-body weights, season and sex affect K (so analysis is stratified by quarter and the Q1 spawning season is checked separately), and length is total length in cm (DATRAS records mm or cm lengths by LngtCode, to be harmonised). Individual weights come from the DATRAS exchange format's CA (age/biological sampling) records, which include IndWgt (g), LngtClass, Maturity and Sex, and Maturity can be used to check where the maturing fraction rises.

dataset.name: DATRAS (Database of Trawl Surveys)
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS holds freely downloadable ICES-coordinated bottom-trawl survey data (e.g. North Sea IBTS and Beam Trawl Survey) including per-fish biological records (CA) with species (Valid_Aphia 127143 for plaice), length class, individual weight, sex and maturity stage. This permits computing K = 100*W/L^3 by length class and locating its maximum relative to the length at which maturity begins.
